subject: Exit-channel accreditation: DNS behavior, NAT pools, and logging for private endpoints
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jmills@acmehealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
Cc: Acme NetOps <netops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — questions on dynamic IPs, DNS and logging

Soojin — thanks for the demo yesterday. NetOps followed up and we have a couple of technical gating items for our private deployment. High level: we need to understand how Redwood's private endpoint will behave from our perimeter perspective. Specifically:

- Will egress originate from a single static IP range for the control plane, or can you support a small dynamic NAT pool per-customer?
- How does Redwood resolve outbound DNS for customer-hosted models (split-horizon concerns)? Do requests perform recursive resolution from inside the VPC or is DNS proxied through Redwood-controlled resolvers?
- We require TLS passthrough (SNI preserved) and no TLS interception — can you confirm?
- Audit/logging ask: we need per-request egress logs (timestamp, src IP, dst FQDN, TLS SNI) for 90 days. What format/endpoint will you provide?

I attached our high-level egress requirements doc. Please loop in engineering/security. We aim to move to an on-prem pilot next month but need these answered for our firewall and procurement signoff.

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
CISO, Acme Health
jmills@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme_netops_egress_requirements.pdf (2.3MB)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — questions on dynamic IPs, DNS and logging

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (networking) and Marissa (customer lead). We'll do a short technical write-up (and propose required firewall rules) but short answers first:

- Redwood Private supports both: a single static egress set (recommended for strict allowlists) or a per-tenant NAT pool (ephemeral but can be scoped to a predictable CIDR). We can propose a NAT-pool size and rotation cadence.
- DNS: by default our runtime performs DNS resolution from inside your VPC (we bind to your VPC DNS path) so split-horizon records resolve as your environment expects. We can also operate via a controlled resolver if required for auditing.
- TLS: we support TLS passthrough with SNI preservation; we do not terminate customer TLS for model traffic unless explicitly configured for hosted routing.
- Logs: we can emit per-request egress records to an S3-compatible endpoint or push to your Syslog/Datadog ingest; format supports JSON lines with timestamp, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_fqdn, sni, model_id, request_id. Retention and delivery method are configurable.

I'll ask David for the NAT pool proposal and Kimberly for the audit controls. Marissa — can you coordinate with Jordan on procurement timeline?

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.example.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 6 Aug 2026 08:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — questions on dynamic IPs, DNS and logging

Folks — quick technical notes and a recommended baseline for Acme: 

1) NAT strategy:
   - Option A (Allowlist-friendly): Allocate a small static CIDR block per-customer (e.g., /29 or /28) and advertise those as egress. Pros: simple firewall rules for customer. Cons: consumes IPs.
   - Option B (Ephemeral NAT pool): Use a managed NAT pool of rotating addresses, bind flows to ephemeral public IPs for the session. Pros: efficient IP usage. Cons: customer firewall must accept rotation and we need a signed assertion of IP mapping over time.

   Recommendation: Offer a hybrid — pinned egress for control plane (static) and optional per-tenant pinned NAT for data plane (customer chooses). For Acme's regulated scope, suggest pinned per-tenant NAT (/29) during pilot; we can revisit for production.

2) DNS behavior:
   - Default is VPC DNS resolution. We do NOT proxy DNS unless requested. This preserves split-horizon and internal hostnames.
   - If Acme wants central logging of DNS lookups, we can forward a copy to your resolver via conditional forwarding.

3) TLS and SNI:
   - Confirming: no TLS interception by default; SNI preserved for passthrough. If TLS termination is required for tooling, that must be explicitly approved and configured.

4) Logging and evidence:
   - We can deliver per-request JSONL records to an S3 bucket you control. Fields: timestamp, request_id, model, src_private_ip, egress_public_ip, dst_ip, dst_fqdn, sni, bytes_sent, bytes_received.
   - For audit the file manifest will include SHA256 of each day's file and we can provide signed attestations on request.

I'll draft a one-pager with proposed CIDR, sample firewall rules (FQDNs + ports), and a sample JSON record. Kimberly — can you confirm if the attestation format we offer matches Acme's compliance needs?

—David
Staff Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@acmehealth.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.example.com, david_kim@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — questions on dynamic IPs, DNS and logging

Jordan — quick note from Security: the attestation and log delivery approach above is acceptable for Acme's SOC-type evidence, with a few caveats:

- We will provide daily manifests signed with our HSM-backed key and include a per-file signature block. That meets integrity requirements for most audits.
- For retention, we can guarantee delivery and indexing for 90 days; if Acme needs Redwood to retain logs beyond that we need a paid retention add-on or a data escrow arrangement.

A couple of requests from our side to make the firewall rules airtight:
- Please whitelist the proposed egress CIDR and also allow outbound DNS (port 53 UDP/TCP) to your resolver endpoints.
- If you choose ephemeral NAT, please allow the /24 prefix associated with the region for fallback during live failover (we'll provide the exact prefix).

If acceptable, we'll produce the signed attestation template and a sample JSONL record by Monday.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from NetOps: 

- For pilot we want pinned per-tenant egress (/29) as you recommended. Please propose the exact /29 CIDR and the expected NAT lifetime (how often will addresses rotate if at all).
- For DNS: we will provide resolver IPs. Please confirm Redwood will do in-VPC resolution against our resolvers and not perform recursive resolution outside our control.
- For logs: S3 delivery to a bucket in our account is preferred. We need sample JSONL and the signing manifest to review with our audit team.

Attached is a terse matrix of the firewall rules we will apply. If you can send the sample JSONL and the signed-manifest example that will let procurement move forward.

—Jordan

Jordan — follow-up and next steps. Deliverables attached/linked: 

1) Proposed CIDR for pilot: 203.0.113.120/29 (egress public IPs 203.0.113.121-126). These will be pinned to your tenant for the pilot with no rotation (90-day pin).
2) DNS: Redwood confirms in-VPC resolution against Acme-provided resolvers. No external recursive resolving by default.
3) Logs: sample JSONL (first line below) and signed manifest example are uploaded to the Drive link and we'll push daily files to the S3 bucket you control. Sample JSONL line:

{"timestamp":"2026-08-11T23:12:45Z","request_id":"req_8a7f2c","model":"redwood-mosaic-v1","src_private_ip":"10.42.5.12","egress_public_ip":"203.0.113.121","dst_ip":"198.51.100.45","dst_fqdn":"api.thirdparty.example.com","sni":"api.thirdparty.example.com","bytes_sent":3450,"bytes_received":1200}

4) Signed manifest: daily file name + SHA256 + HSM signature. We'll provide the template and an example signed blob by end of day tomorrow.

5) Ops runbook: David will share a minimal firewall snippet (FQDN + port list) and I will set up the initial cross-account S3 delivery permissions. Marissa — please confirm pilot start date so we can schedule the work.

If that aligns, we will prepare the formal attestation packet and a short checklist for your NetOps. Happy to schedule a 30-min call to walk through.

—Soojin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
